target_customer: Women trying to conceive who test hormones at home
problem: Home ovulation tests only detect a single hormone surge; Zergo claimed a sensor could read fertility hormones in urine more precisely to help women time conception.
business_model: Consumer hardware: reusable or disposable urine sensor plus consumables
product_category: Fertility tech hardware, electrochemical urine hormone sensor

founders.name: Thomas Dunlop
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page; no bio found.

founders.name: Noah Debrincat
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as a previous founder of Zergo (S19); no bio found.

exit.reason: Cause not public; YC lists the company as Inactive and the domain is parked for sale.

technical_complexity.rationale: A new electrochemical sensor reading hormones in urine needs hardware design, assay validation and regulatory clearance from a team of nine; an aggregator says the team reused a sensor first built for a cannabis breathalyzer.

defensibility.rationale: Sensor IP and any FDA clearance would be hard to copy, but one aggregator reports no 510(k), PMA or device registration under Zergo in openFDA searches, so no regulatory moat was shown.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Zergo; the company simply went inactive.

market_need_then: Demand for home fertility testing was established in 2019, with consumer hormone monitors on the market, but no Zergo specific traction data was found.

branding.domain_note: Used the exact .com zergo.com; the domain now redirects to a GoDaddy for sale page (checked 2026-11).

brand_strength.rationale: Searches found no press, community or brand material about the Zergo name; the brand left almost no public trace.

outcome_analysis: Zergo was a nine person Waterloo hardware startup that joined YC in Summer 2019 and reportedly raised about 150 thousand dollars. The cause of its end is not public, so failure factors are left empty. A secondary profile suggests the team reused a cannabis breathalyzer sensor for fertility hormones, but it shows no regulatory clearance, and the company is listed Inactive with its domain parked.
notes: The seed round rests on a single database (Seedtable, which also gives an estimated 75/25 split between lead and YC that is not confirmed). The search results for a dated competitor set returned nothing about Zergo, so the list is empty. An aggregator (healthcarediscovery.ai) says the company was earlier called SannTek Labs and built a breath test; this is unverified and its history is partly garbled. Company website is dead (domain for sale).
